เรื่องเล่าที่บันทึกโดย Gplace ระบุว่า ชา: An account recorded by Gplace says that Hokkien Chinese people who came to mine in Khlong Pi community joined together to build a Guan Yu shrine, with Lim Bun Tuek involved in its founding, and began a nine-day, nine-night Vegetarian Festival ritual in 1843 CE. The same source spells personal names inconsistently, and no primary evidence has been found, so this should be read as an origin legend, not a verified year
ฉากหลังของตะกั่วป่าในเวลานั้นคือเมืองชาย: At that time, Takua Pa was a coastal town growing through tin mining and Hokkien Chinese merchant networks. The shrine therefore likely served both as a home for the community's protective deity and as a ritual centre for miners and merchants. This is consistent with the municipality's description that the shrine arose from Hokkien Chinese faith and was the origin of Takua Pa's Vegetarian Festival, but the year and builder have not been verified in academic documents.

Gplace เล่าว่าศาลถูกย้ายจากชุมชนคลองปีไป: Gplace says the shrine was moved from Khlong Pi community to a permanent site at Ban Chae Lim in Talat Yai, and that funds were raised to buy a house in 1902 CE by Lim Eng Cheng, or Tao Kae Pho Daeng. However, no evidence has been found confirming the building date or transfer of ownership, so that year should not be treated as the construction year of the current shrine
หลักฐานที่พบอธิบายบทบาทของสถานที่ต่อเนื่: The evidence found describes continuity in the site's role rather than a change of function: the shrine remains tied to Takua Pa's Vegetarian Festival, which has been passed down among Thai people of Chinese descent on the Andaman coast, and later became part of the Talat Yai old-town landscape. At the same time, no online evidence has been found confirming any restoration, abandonment, direct impact from the 2004 tsunami, or registration of this shrine as a historic site.
หลักฐานข่าวล่าสุดที่พบยืนยันการใช้งานศาล: The latest news evidence found confirms the shrine's use as Talat Tai's vegetarian-festival shrine: on 2 October 2024, a Ko Teng pole-raising ceremony was held there to begin the Vegetarian Festival. The hanging of nine lanterns and continuing ceremonies show that the shrine remains a centre of community faith and shared activities, not merely an old building in the market area

Contact the community or municipality before travelling. Based on the information available, the shrine is near the junction of Thanon Udom Thara and Thanon Si Takua Pa in the Talat Yai area, and the confirmed activities are the Vegetarian Festival and the Ko Teng pole-raising ceremony.

เรื่องของสะพานเริ่มขึ้นในเมืองตะกั่วป่าย: The bridge's story began in Takua Pa during the tin-mining era, when the Boonsung dredging company stood on the opposite bank from the old market. The Takua Pa canal was more than 40 metres wide, so workers and residents had to row across, especially when floodwaters rose. The local database of Prince of Songkla University states that mining operator Juti Boonsung therefore first initiated a wooden bridge for walking and cycling
ต่อมาใน พ.ศ. 2511 มีการนำเหล็กจากเรือขุด: Later, in 1968 CE (2511 BE), steel from a decommissioned dredger was assembled into Khok Khanuen Iron Bridge, more than 200 metres long, across the Takua Pa River. The bridge was therefore not only industrial infrastructure, but also a shortcut for workers, a goods route, and a daily connection between the old market and the town's tin-driven mining area. Verifiable evidence confirms the mining and transport roles, but no contemporary document has been found directly linking this bridge to details about maritime trade, Hokkien Chinese people, or the town-governor system
หลัง พ.ศ. 2511-ก่อน พ.ศ. 2569 / ค.ศ. 196: After 1968 CE (2511 BE) and before 2026 CE (2569 BE)
เมื่อกิจการเหมืองแร่ยุติลง สะพานไม่ได้หา: When mining ended, the bridge did not disappear with the dredging plant. It changed from a work structure into a community route and evidence of the industrial landscape. ONEP sources state that the old dredging plant, preserved in its original condition, can still be seen from the bridge area, while contemporary tourism sources call the bridge a symbol of Takua Pa's mining-town past
ในช่วงต่อมา สะพานถูกเล่าและนำเสนอเป็นจุด: Later, the bridge was described and presented as a tourist and photography spot, and it also appeared as a location in the film Wonderful Town (2007), according to an article tracking filming locations. However, this review found no evidence confirming when the mine closed, when major repairs took place, any direct impact from the 2004 tsunami, or registration as a historic site by the Fine Arts Department. These events should therefore not be added as facts
ปัจจุบันสะพานเหล็กบุญสูงยังทำหน้าที่เป็น: Today, Boonsung Iron Bridge still serves as a community route. Field information and reviews say that residents use it for travel and motorcycles pass through. At the same time, Takua Pa Municipality classifies it as a tourist attraction, and a TAT tourism source has current images of the site. The bridge thus stands between functioning infrastructure and a landmark for walking, views, and photography
หลักฐานล่าสุดที่พบคือข่าว NBT วันที่ 30: The latest evidence found is an NBT report dated 30 January 2026, which introduces the bridge as mining heritage associated with Takua Pa and says it was temporarily closed at that time to accommodate a foreign film shoot. In addition, a municipal budget document found includes items for maintaining and improving the bridge entrance area, but no document has been found confirming a restoration project for the structure itself. Opening and closing hours, admission fees, an activity-specific custodian, and the latest safety condition therefore still need to be checked on site
